title: Fix Windows installation crashes and define ARM64 support limits
description:
MarkItDown imports ONNX Runtime during installation. Newer ONNX Runtime wheels crash on CRAN's Windows builders, and native Windows ARM64 lacks working dependencies for document conversion and DuckDB stores.

- Require `onnxruntime<=1.20.1` on Windows to keep document conversion working on the affected builders.
- Keep eager Python cache warm-up in a child process so native import failures remain visible without aborting installation.
- On native Windows ARM64, decline MarkItDown conversion and DuckDB stores before initialization, while leaving package loading and Markdown chunking available. Document the remaining upstream reticulate limitation.

Adds regression coverage for the ARM64 gates, installation with a crashing warm-up, and real public HTML conversion. The installation regression runs in Windows CI.

Win-builder release (R 4.6.2, Windows Server 2022 x64) passed warm-up and both public conversion probes: 434 passing assertions, no errors or warnings, and one NOTE for the development version and a rate-limited ROR URL. The local full suite retains the existing Atlas terminal-handle import error; oldrel/devel results are pending.

Related to #215 and #213.

title: Treat document origins literally in ingest progress

title: Read sitemap timestamps and optionally return link metadata
description:
`ragnar_find_links()` reads `<lastmod>` dates and datetimes from sitemap `<urlset>` entries without extra requests, preserving time zones and fractional seconds. With `get_timestamps = TRUE`, URLs without a usable sitemap date follow the existing HEAD-request path. Dates stay aligned with normalized URLs and survive crawling or redirects when the page omits `Last-Modified`.

The new opt-in `metadata = TRUE` returns a tibble with `source` and `last_modified` columns, so timestamps stay with their links through joins and row-binding. The default remains a `ragnar_links` character vector. Both forms retain crawl diagnostics in the `problems` attribute, with the documented `link` and `problem` columns. Missing or non-HTTP(S) sitemap locations are excluded and reported there.

Closes #211.

Validation: all 42 assertions in the new sitemap, metadata, and diagnostic test files pass against the installed package. Combined installed-package tests with #210 also pass, including default-link ingestion and metadata-to-audit workflows. The full macOS package check reached 758 passing assertions, with five callr session-start timeouts in webfakes fixtures before the tested code ran and five credential-dependent skips; there were no warnings or notes.

title: feat(store): add ragnar_store_audit() for coverage reporting (#203)
description:
`ragnar_store_audit()` checks an expected set of URLs or file paths against a version 2 store after ingestion. It returns one summary row, or one row per `group_by` value, with distinct expected, ingested, and missing counts, stored chunk counts, and a `missing_urls` list-column.

`expected` accepts a character vector, `ragnar_links`, or a data frame with a `source` column. Duplicate origins count once per group; origins outside the expected set are excluded. Empty inputs and read-only connections are supported. The store schema is unchanged.

`ragnar_store_ingest()` batches modification-time comparisons in DuckDB to recognize unchanged files at half-microsecond boundaries across DuckDB versions. The retrieval memory test reads both DuckDB 1.x and 2.0 profiles, keeping its existing scan-cardinality and memory limits.

Closes #203.

Validation: 185 focused installed-package assertions pass on each of DuckDB 1.5.6 and 2.0.0, covering incremental ingestion, HTTP and file freshness, retrieval memory limits, store auditing, and constant query counts for unchanged ingestion, with no warnings or skips. The full macOS `R CMD check --no-manual` with DuckDB 2.0.0 passes with 758 assertions, 7 skipped tests, and no errors, warnings, or notes.

With DuckDB 2.0.0 and one database thread, re-ingesting the same 1,000 unchanged local files with indexing disabled takes a median 0.018 seconds, compared with 0.024 seconds at the merge base (15 measured calls after 3 warmups per implementation; setup and initial ingestion excluded).

title: Fix `markdown_chunk()` with combining characters
description:
`markdown_node_positions()` built its byte-to-char offset table from grapheme clusters, which merge a base character with a following combining mark (NFD-normalized text) into one unit — undercounting relative to the code-point-based `stri_length()`/`stri_sub()` used elsewhere in the chunker, so offsets after a combining sequence were wrong.

The fix builds the table from code points instead (`utf8ToInt()` plus per-code-point UTF-8 byte lengths), matching `stri_length()`/`stri_sub()`.

Added a regression test in `tests/testthat/test-chunk.R` with an NFD-decomposed heading and paragraph; it fails on base and passes with the fix.

Fixes #158.

title: feat(ingest): incremental ingest via Last-Modified/content hash and ragnar_store_sync() (#200, #201)
description:
## Summary

- **Freshness columns** added to the v2 `documents` table (`last_modified TIMESTAMPTZ`, `content_hash VARCHAR`, `ingested_at TIMESTAMPTZ`).
- **Incremental ingest** (#200): `ragnar_store_ingest()` now skips unchanged pages. For HTTP URLs, issues a HEAD request first (cheap); if `Last-Modified` is present, uses it. Otherwise uses `rlang::hash()` of the prepared Markdown. For local files, uses `file.mtime()`. Successfully ingested pages update these columns for future comparisons. `ingest_summary` gains a `"skipped_unchanged"` status.
- **`ragnar_store_sync()`** (#201): removes stale documents from a v2 store. Accepts a character vector of URLs to keep; deletes everything else (embeddings + documents) atomically via `dbWithTransaction2()`. `dry_run = TRUE` returns a preview tibble without modifying the store. Returns `store` invisibly with a `sync_summary` attribute.

## Notes

- FK constraint removed from `embeddings.doc_id`: DuckDB 1.x does not support deferred FK checking inside a transaction. Referential integrity is enforced by application code (delete embeddings before documents).
- Existing v2 stores must be recreated with `ragnar_store_create()`; no automatic migration is provided.
- `ragnar_store_update()` replaces shortened documents even when all remaining chunks are already stored. Passing a subset of an unchanged document retains its other chunks.

title: feat(ingest): attach ingest_summary attribute to ragnar_store_ingest() return value
description:
## Summary

Closes #202.

`ragnar_store_ingest()` now returns `store` invisibly with an `ingest_summary` attribute: a tibble with columns `path` (character), `status` (character), `n_chunks` (integer), and `message` (character).

- `"ok"` -- path was processed successfully
- `"skipped_exists"` -- origin was already in the store; not re-dispatched to workers
- `"error"` -- worker failed (warning issued as before via `rlang::warn()`)

The summary has one row per input path, in input order. `n_chunks` is the stored chunk count for the document's origin after ingestion (`0L` for errors), and `message` is the worker error message (`NA` otherwise). Duplicate paths are processed once.

### Behaviour change: skipped_exists paths are no longer re-dispatched

Previously, paths where `is_new_origin = FALSE` were still sent to mirai workers (they just skipped the embedding step). They are now short-circuited before any worker is launched and recorded immediately as `"skipped_exists"`. This avoids re-preparing documents that are already stored.

`build_index = TRUE` builds the requested indexes even when all paths already exist. Freshness checks and re-ingestion of changed documents are handled separately in #209.

### Worker error handling

Worker errors continue to use `rlang::warn(..., class = "ragnar_ingest_worker_error", path = path)`. The failed input path and error message are also recorded in `ingest_summary`.

title: fix(ingest): correct n_workers formula (#206) and emit structured worker-error conditions (#205)
description:
## Summary

Fixes two bugs in `ragnar_store_ingest()`:

- **#206** — The default `n_workers` formula used `max(detectCores(), 4L)` where `min` was intended. On machines with fewer than 4 cores this over-allocated workers.

- **#205** — Worker errors were emitted as bare `warning(cond)`, giving callers no structured signal and no programmatic way to identify which URL failed or handle it selectively. This is a correctness problem for any caller recording per-page metadata after ingest (e.g. caching `Last-Modified` timestamps): a failed page's metadata could be recorded, causing it to be silently skipped on all future runs.

## Changes

**`R/ingest.R`**

- Corrected the `n_workers` default formula to `max(2L, min(n_cores, n_paths %/% 4L, 8L))`, using four cores if `detectCores()` is unavailable. Updated the docstring to match.
- Replaced `warning(cond)` with `rlang::warn(..., class = "ragnar_ingest_worker_error", path = <url>)` so callers can catch it with `withCallingHandlers()` and inspect the failed path programmatically.
- Kept each task's path with its queued result so the path is available when an error is collected in the main process, including invalid preparation results, worker interruptions, and worker exits.
- Handle R errors, interruptions, and transport failures separately so each produces a useful warning and ingest continues.
- Removed two leftover `# browser()` comments (development scaffolding noted in #205).

**`DESCRIPTION`**

- Added `nanonext` as a direct import for transport error messages; it is already a dependency of `mirai`.

Updated the help page and release notes to match the worker defaults and warning fields. The regression tests cover representative core and page counts, unavailable core detection, the warning class and failed path, and continued ingestion after errors, interruptions, and worker exits through the public API.

## Related issues

Closes #205, closes #206.

title: feat(find-links): make root URL inclusion opt-in
description:

- When enabled, seeds `collected` with `start_url` before the crawl loop begins, so the root is included subject to filtering and validation; sitemap inputs return only their listed pages
- The opt-in behavior mirrors how [raghilda](https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda) handles this: the root is placed in the frontier and yielded when fetched, like any other page

Fixes #198

title: feat(find-links): return Last-Modified timestamps and ragnar_links print method
description:

- Existing callers that ignore attributes are unaffected; the return type is still a character vector
- HEAD requests use `req_error(is_error = \(resp) FALSE)` and a 10 s timeout so HTTP errors do not surface as noise

title: Reduce VSS retrieval memory use
description:
Reduce VSS retrieval memory use by ranking physical row IDs and fetching embeddings and document text for the final matches. Indexed filters read at most 5,000 HNSW candidates before selecting those matches. The SQL changes retain API signatures and support custom `rowid` columns.

Retrieval uses fixed `metric_name` and `metric_value` columns. Metadata using either name, ignoring case, now causes an error asking users to create a store with different metadata column names. VSS, BM25, and combined retrieval share this check instead of generating alternate metric names.

Filters can use document fields and computed metric columns and respect `top_k` across the candidate boundary. Store creation and connection disable insertion-order preservation. The documentation explains deployment-specific memory limits and allocations outside those limits. Requires DuckDB >= 1.5.0 for bounded row-ID fetches.

Validation: 360 focused retrieval and store assertions pass; the full suite passes 441 assertions with six skips. `R CMD check --no-manual --ignore-vignettes` reports 0 errors, 0 warnings, and 0 notes on DuckDB 1.5.6. Coverage includes metric-name conflicts, case variants, reconnected stores, BM25-only stores, custom `rowid` fields, indexed scan bounds, and bounded-memory retrieval.

Benchmarks compare `main` (`84cbd18`) with this PR (`5f66194`) on an Apple M4 Max, R 4.6.1, and DuckDB 1.5.6. Synthetic version 2 stores have one source document each and random embeddings. Queries call `ragnar_retrieve_vss()` with one thread, `top_k = 3`, Euclidean distance, a supplied query vector, and insertion-order preservation disabled on both revisions. Times are medians across 14 warm batches in two fresh processes; indexed batches contain 20 queries.

For an unindexed filtered search over 18,000 chunks with 1,024 dimensions, with `memory_limit = '2GB'`:

| Measure                               |    main |      PR |
| ------------------------------------- | ------: | ------: |
| Public API query time                 |  389 ms | 45.2 ms |
| Peak DuckDB buffers                   | 945 MiB | 239 MiB |
| Peak process RSS, including R startup | 910 MiB | 412 MiB |

This case is about 8.6× faster, with 75% lower peak buffers and 55% lower peak RSS. At a 128 MB DuckDB limit, main runs out of memory and the PR succeeds; at 64 MB, both run out of memory.

For 200,000 chunks with 128 dimensions and an HNSW index built before setting the 32 MB query budget, unfiltered warm queries take **3.37 ms on main versus 4.80 ms on the PR**, a 42% slowdown. Filtered queries run out of memory on main and complete in about 100 ms on the PR. A separate cold-start test on a store with three persisted HNSW indexes exceeded 32 MB on both revisions. These measurements support the large filtered-query improvement while showing the overhead for small indexed results. Successful comparable runs returned the same chunks, embeddings, and scores.

Fixes #188.

title: Reserve retrieval column names in store schemas
description:
Reserve `rowid`, `metric_name`, `metric_value`, and the `_ragnar_` prefix for retrieval, ignoring case. Store creation rejects these names before overwriting a file; connection rejects existing schemas containing them. Existing stores must rename those metadata columns before reconnecting. Public retrieval fields remain `metric_name` and `metric_value`.

Rename temporary de-overlap columns to use `_ragnar_`, so metadata named `overlap_grp` and `deoverlapped_id` is preserved. This PR establishes the naming contract independently of the VSS memory changes in #189.

Validation: public API regressions cover both store versions, case variants, existing stores, overwrite protection, and metadata preservation. Focused store and retrieval tests pass; `R CMD check --no-manual --ignore-vignettes` reports 0 errors, 0 warnings, and 0 notes with DuckDB 1.5.6.

title: fix(read-html): skip URLs already queued in ragnar_find_links()
description:
Fixes #192.

The crawl loop only checked `visited` (pages already fetched) before enqueuing child links, not whether a URL was already waiting in the deque. On sites with cross-linked navigation — a sidebar appearing on every page is the common case — every depth-2 URL gets enqueued once per depth-1 page that references it. On `https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/` this inflated a ~400-URL crawl into ~20,000 HTTP requests.

## The fix

Add a `queued` set that tracks URLs the moment they enter the deque. Before appending, both `visited` and `queued` are now checked.

```r
if (!visited$`__contains__`(link) && !queued$`__contains__`(link)) {
  deque$append(list(url = link, depth = item$depth + 1))
  queued$add(link)
}
```

## Benchmark

URL: `https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/`, `children_only = TRUE`

| depth | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1,005s | 30s | 33x |
| 3 | would not terminate | 28s | |

Link counts are identical before and after. All existing tests pass.

title: add `ragnar_store_ingest()`
description:
The primary motivation for this function is to speed up store creation using parallelism. It offloads the work of reading, converting to markdown, chunking, and generating embeddings to mirai background workers. This substantially reduces store creation time. For example, creating a store from `quarto.org` processes about 90% of the site in \~20 seconds before hitting a TPM rate limit of 1 million tokens per minute with OpenAI. Previously it would take around 10 minutes total. 

This will require a solution for rate-limit handling, either through smart backoff or support for using the batch API. ~~These can be addressed in follow-up PRs.~~ 

We now disable the background workers from retrying the request after a 429. The main thread then tries to generate embeddings with retries, and blocks until the embedding request succeeds. This gracefully leads to backpressure and lets the whole queue be rate-limited without spamming excessive retries.

title: MCP ragnar server
description:
Expose a helper that lets users expose a ragnar store as an MCP server to clients. 

E.g., if using Codex, you could add an entry like this to `~/.codex/config.toml`

```toml
[mcp_servers.quartohelp]
command = "Rscript"
args = ["-e", "ragnar::mcp_serve_store(quartohelp:::quartohelp_store_path())"]
```

Then the `codex` app will be able to search the store:

title: Inspector updates
description:
Misc fixes and improvements to the Store Inspector.

## Changes

### Layout and Navigation

* Updated app header layout to reduce vertical space and increase content area.
* Enlarged search input area.
* Added documents count to subheader.
* Increased default results cap to **100**.
* Added draggable split between Documents and Preview:

  * Defaults to golden ratio (\~38.2% / 61.8%).
  * Focusable separator with keyboard resize:

    * Left/Right arrows (Shift for larger steps).
    * `g`/Home to reset.

* Added ARIA attributes for accessibility.

### Documents List

* Selection persists across re-renders if item remains present.
* Keyboard navigation:

  * ArrowUp/ArrowDown or `j`/`k` to change selection.
  * List is focusable.

### Search UX

* Shortcuts:

  * `/` focuses search.
  * `Esc` clears search.

### Preview

* **Markdown Preview**:

  * Fixed linkifying issues (errors, false positives, false negatives).
  * No longer linkify tibble truncated urls that end with `…`
  * Fix warning from stringi
 
* **Raw Text**:

  * Added soft-wrap for long lines (`whitespace-pre-wrap + break-words`).

### Metadata and Context

* Fixed metadata/context not displaying with `store@version == 2`.
* Stopped using `store@schema`.

### Code and Dependency Fixes

* Namespaced all `shiny::` calls for fixes when running without `ragnar` dev-loaded.
* Conslidated `class` attributes in Document rows.
* Fixed references to invalid or non-existant Tailwind classes.

One of the CRAN test server is a Linux machine with R compiled

title: Delegate requests to httr2
description:
This is a draft PR for discussion. The idea here is to centralize all requests made by ragnar to use httr2 and add a callback allowing users to modify requests. This allows users to use a central cache that can be shared for both finding links and reading documents. It also allows users to modify requests such that they can be retried, have a timeout, etc.

Here's an example:

```
modify_request <- function(req) {
  req |>
    httr2::req_cache(path = "cache")
}


links <- ragnar::ragnar_find_links(
  "https://quarto.org",
  depth = 3,
  children_only = FALSE,
  url_filter = function(x) {
    # We only want quarto links from official repositories
    # - quarto.org
    stringi::stri_subset(x, regex = "^https://quarto.org")
  },
  modify_request = modify_request
)
```

Then links can be read with:

```
doc <- link |>
      ragnar::ragnar_read(
        frame_by_tags = "h1",
        modify_request = modify_request
      )
```

Another idea, would be for `find_links` to return `httr2_response` objects (eg being something very similar to what ragnar_perform_spider() would do https://github.com/r-lib/httr2/issues/456. And `ragnar_read` being able to read `httr2_response` objects additionally.

title: Implement ragnar store version 2 with support for deoverlapping and automatic augmentation
description:
This PR introduces a new store version with support for:

* Deoverlapping chunks on retrieval
* Automatic chunk augmentation with in-scope markdown headings

### Ingestion Changes

Most changes are internal; typical users can upgrade easily.
**Update ingestion pipelines:**
Replace

```r
path |> ragnar_read() |> ragnar_chunk() |> glue(<augment>)
```

with

```r
path |> read_as_markdown() |> markdown_chunk()
```

Results should improve with the new pipeline.

If your workflow relies on the previous schema, you can maintain compatibility by specifying the earlier store version:

```r
ragnar_store_create(..., version = 1)
```

### Retrieval Changes

* Usage of `tbl(store)` with `ragnar_retrieve()` is deprecated.
* For common cases, supply a filter expression directly to `ragnar_retrieve()`.
* For more advanced queries, access the underlying store connection directly via the new property `store@con` and write your own dplyr expressions or SQL.
* `ragnar_retrieve_vss()` method choices has been updated to a narrower set to ensure that the HNSW index scan is used. Only `cosine_distance`, `euclidean_distance` and `negative_inner_product` are supported. The remaining set of metrics (`cosine_similarity`,  `inner_product`, `dot_product` are alises or simple linear transforms of the other methods, but do not support an index scan and are no longer accepted.

### Other Improvements

* `ragnar_store_create(extra_cols)` now supports additional column types, including date and datetime.
* `ragnar_register_tool_retrieve()` now returns a dataframe directly (ellmer serializes this as a row-oriented JSON list); previously, only chunk text was returned.
* retrieval functions now support additional options:
  - All functions now take a `filter` expression argument
  - `ragnar_retrieve_bm25()` gains arguments `b`, `k`, and `conjunctive`.
  - `ragnar_retrieve_vss()` takes arguments `embed_vector`, supporting workflows that preprocess the search string before embedding.
  - `ragnar_retrieve()` now passes along `...` to all underlying methods
  - `ragnar_retrieve()` will automatically deoverlap retrieved chunks.
* Default model for `embed_ollama` is now `"snowflake-arctic-embed2:568m"`. The embed function choice is now recorded in store metadata, so future changes in the model default will not break previously created stores.
* `embed_ollama` provides better error messages (e.g., vector length too large, model not installed, etc.).
* `markdown_chunk()` returns a classed S7 object: `MarkdownDocumentChunks`. This is the same tibble as before, just with additional S7 properties. 
* Fixed an issue with chunking documents that have no markdown headings.
* Adds a `configure` script to enable `read_as_markdown()` examples to run on CRAN by pre-configuring the reticulate dependencies. 
* Additional work is in place to ensure that the HNSW index is used for VSS search, even when filter expressions are supplied (previously, a `filter` expression forced a sequential scan).


### Background

This branch started as an exploration of deoverlapping support, initially assuming it would be incompatible with the previous transparent approach to chunking and reading. The original plan was to implement a high-level function, `ragnar_store_ingest()`, to manage chunking, augmentation, deoverlapping, and rechunking. This proved unnecessary, so the approach was refactored to introduce a new store version.

Longer-term, I would like to support an `RCodeBase` document type, allowing chunking and rechunking powered by [flowr-analysis/flowr](https://github.com/flowr-analysis/flowr). For this reason, ingestion classes are specialized on Markdown (`MarkdownDocument` and `MarkdownDocumentChunks`), and I've avoided introducing an abstract `Document` or `DocumentChunks` class that assumes chunks correspond to line ranges.

### New Exports

* `MarkdownDocument`
* `MarkdownDocumentChunks`
* `chunks_deoverlap`


### Issue References

* Closes #58: `ragnar_retrieve_bm25` gains new arguments (`b`, `k`, `conjunctive`)
* #39: Adds support for overlapping chunks
* Partially fixes #36: No longer warns about missing ‘hash’ column; document hash is not required with store version 2

title: Add `markdown_chunk()`
description:
This implements a new chunker for Markdown documents. It:

* Automatically adjusts chunk boundaries to nearby semantic boundaries (headings, paragraphs, sentences, lines, or words) to minimize awkward breaks.
* Adds a `headings` column with the in-scope headings at each chunk start (this supersedes the previous `frame_by_tags` approach).
* Ensures the last chunk in a document or segment is not an excessively small outlier by anchoring the chunk end to the document boundary and selecting the chunk start position based on the target chunk size (potentially introducing overlap).
* Allows specifying a desired chunk overlap percentage.
* Allows specifying that some Markdown heading levels should be hard segment breaks.

This partially addresses #39.

`````markdown
## Caching

The [Knitr Cache](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/cache.html) operates at the level of individual cells rather than the entire document. While this can be very convenient, it also introduced some special requirements around managing the dependencies between cells.

You can enable the Knitr cache at the document or project level using standard YAML options:

``` yaml
---
title: "My Document"
format: html
execute:
  cache: true
---
```

You can also enable caching on a per-cell basis (in this you would *not* set the document level option):

```` markdown
```{r}
#| cache: true

summary(cars)
```
````

title: feat(tool): Adds tool annotations
description:
The core goal of this PR is to add tool annotations to the tool definition created in `ragnar_register_tool_retrieve()` to communicate that the tools are read-only and not open-world tools. It's also helpful to have a `title` annotation (i.e. a friendly name instead of `rag_retrieve_from_001`).

I added `name` and `title` as params to `ragnar_register_tool_retrieve()` that default to the name and title from the `store` (it's also useful to choose the name and title when registering the tool).

To make things easier, I added `title` to `ragnar_store_create()`  and `RagnarStore()` so that it's stored next to `name`. I can walk this change back if you want.

Here's a simple example based on the r4ds example in the README

``` r
pkgload::load_all()
#> ℹ Loading ragnar

store_location <- tempfile(fileext = ".ragnar.duckdb")

store <- ragnar_store_create(
  store_location,
  embed = ragnar::embed_ollama(model = "nomic-embed-text"),
  name = "r4ds",
  title = "R for Data Science (2e)"
)

store@name
#> [1] "r4ds"
store@title
#> [1] "R for Data Science (2e)"

chat <- ellmer::chat_ollama(model = "granite3.2:8b")
ragnar_register_tool_retrieve(chat, store)

chat$get_tools()
#> $rag_retrieve_from_r4ds
#> <ellmer::ToolDef>
#>  @ name       : 'glue' chr "rag_retrieve_from_r4ds"
#>  @ fun        : function (text)  
#>  @ description: 'glue' chr "Given a string, retrieve the most relevent excerpts from the knowledge store."
#>  @ arguments  : <ellmer::TypeObject>
#>  .. @ description          : NULL
#>  .. @ required             : logi TRUE
#>  .. @ properties           :List of 1
#>  .. .. $ text: <ellmer::TypeBasic>
#>  .. ..  ..@ description: chr "The text to find the most relevent matches for."
#>  .. ..  ..@ required   : logi TRUE
#>  .. ..  ..@ type       : chr "string"
#>  .. @ additional_properties: logi FALSE
#>  @ convert    : logi TRUE
#>  @ annotations:List of 3
#>  .. $ title          : chr "R for Data Science (2e)"
#>  .. $ read_only_hint : logi TRUE
#>  .. $ open_world_hint: logi FALSE

chat$set_tools(list())
ragnar_register_tool_retrieve(
  chat,
  store,
  name = "search_r4ds",
  title = "Search R for Data Science (2e)"
)
chat$get_tools()
#> $search_r4ds
#> <ellmer::ToolDef>
#>  @ name       : chr "search_r4ds"
#>  @ fun        : function (text)  
#>  @ description: 'glue' chr "Given a string, retrieve the most relevent excerpts from the knowledge store."
#>  @ arguments  : <ellmer::TypeObject>

title: Enhancments to `read_as_markdown()`
description:
While building quartohelp, I noticed two issues with `read_as_markdown()` output. These were annoying enough that I used `pandoc::pandoc_convert()` instead in the initial draft.

1. The returned markdown included navigational elements from the sidebar, page header, and footer. For short pages, these could dominate the document chunks. As a result, many retrieved chunks were mostly or entirely navigational elements. This PR changes the behavior so that, by default for HTML documents, `read_as_markdown()` will exclude any content outside of the `main` tag if one is present.

2. If a pre-formatted code block contained a markdown fence ` ``` `, it confused post-processing or rendering of chunks (e.g., in the `ragnar_store_inspect()`). This PR increases the outermost fence to the necessary number of backticks to ensure the output chunk is valid markdown. For example, previously chunks might be formatted like this:
    `````
    ```
    ```{r}
    foo
    ```
    ```
    `````
    and after this PR are now converted to:
    `````
    ````
    ```{r}
    foo
    ```
    ````
    `````

title: Refactor `ragnar_find_links`

title: Add support for `update` when inserting documents into the store
description:
Follow up for https://github.com/t-kalinowski/ragnar/pull/2

This PR now uses `origin` and `hash` introduced in #2 to identify which documents need to be updated when calling
`ragnar_store_insert()`. The basic mechanism is:

When you insert a chunks data frame containing `origin` and `hash` columns we now:

1. Check the store if there's already some documents with the same `origin` and `hash`, if there's we filter them out and don't try to insert them again.
2. If the origin exists, but the hash is different: we delete all chunks with that origin and insert the new chunks.
3. If the origin is new, we insert all new chunks.

title: Store failing URLs in `problems`
description:
Fixes #3 

With this PR, failures when trying to 'find links' from a URL will instead get saved in a `problems` tibble that's returned to the user as an attribute of `ragnar_find_links`, so they can inspect and understand what are the errors.

Additionally, this PR works around a problem in `url_absolute()` that will destroy some URL's (specially if they contain spaces) and transform them into `NA`, making the `problems` database less useful. Now, if for some reason, `url_absolute()` returns NA, we replace back with the original link and try to read it later using both the original URL and its encoded version.

title: Allow webfakes app processes more time to start in tests
description:
Tests that serve a local site with `webfakes::new_app_process()` fail intermittently on R-universe's macOS x86_64 builders with `webfakes app subprocess did not start :(`. webfakes waits 5 seconds by default for each app subprocess to start, and these runners sometimes take longer.

This adds `tests/testthat/setup-webfakes.R`, which sets `R_WEBFAKES_PROCESS_TIMEOUT` to 60 seconds for the test run. The limit only matters when startup is slow, so passing runs take no longer.

This is a test-only change; there are no user-facing changes.

Related to #213. The other macOS x86_64 failure mode in that issue (timeouts while R-universe compiles duckdb 2.0.0 from source) comes from R-universe's dependency step and is not addressed here.

## Testing

- With `R_WEBFAKES_PROCESS_TIMEOUT=1` set externally, `test-find-links.R` fails with the same error seen in CI before this change and passes after it, because the setup file overrides the value.
- The full local test suite passes.

title: Warn when calling deprecated read and chunk functions

## User-facing changes

- The `ragnar_store_create()` docs now recommend `read_as_markdown()` and `markdown_chunk()` for preparing `version = 1` chunks. The `ragnar_chunks_view()` docs now refer to `markdown_chunk()` instead of `ragnar_read()`.
- NEWS entry added.

## Internal changes

- New snapshot test covering the warnings from the chunking functions. The `ragnar_read()` tests now expect or silence the warning.
- roxygen2 version bumped to 8.1.1 in `DESCRIPTION`.

## Testing

`devtools::test()`: 870 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings, 5 skipped.

title: Prepare ragnar 0.4.0 release
description:
Prepare ragnar 0.4.0 for release. The version is bumped to 0.4.0, and the development NEWS is grouped into breaking changes, new features, and improvements and fixes. The new deprecation warnings for `ragnar_read()`, `ragnar_chunk()`, `ragnar_segment()`, and `ragnar_chunk_segments()` (#219) are listed under breaking changes. The README is rebuilt with DuckDB 2.0, updating the example output. The CRAN comments explain the ROR URL note and describe the Windows installation changes and the reverse dependency check.

For the README build, explicitly set DuckDB's storage location and disconnect the writable store before the read-only retrieval example. These changes affect the build setup, not the package API.

Tests that start a webfakes server now go through a `local_app_process()` helper that skips on CRAN. webfakes starts its subprocess with callr's fixed 3-second startup timeout, which a loaded check machine can exceed.

Public-facing changes are limited to the version number and documentation: NEWS, README, and CRAN comments. The test change is internal, and there are no package code changes beyond what is already on `main`.

## Testing

- `devtools::check(remote = TRUE, manual = TRUE)` on macOS with DuckDB 2.0.0: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 note (the ROR URL returning 429, explained in `cran-comments.md`).
- win-builder R-release (4.6.2): 1 note, the same ROR URL.
- With `CRAN=true`, the test suite starts no webfakes servers.
- `devtools::test()` with DuckDB 1.5.6, the version CRAN's macOS x86_64 binaries provide: all tests pass.
- R CMD check of commons against CRAN ragnar 0.3.1 and this branch: both `Status: OK` with identical test results.
- `devtools::check_win_devel()` was submitted for 0.4.0; results are pending.

Related to #215.

title: Automatically upgrade older v2 stores on writable connections
description:
Allow older v2 stores to open without recreation.

### Public-facing changes

Read-only connections open older v2 stores without changing them. Writable connections upgrade the schema on disk. Existing documents have unknown freshness and are reprocessed when their sources are next ingested; later runs can skip unchanged sources. Store synchronization can remove documents after the upgrade.

### Internal changes

The upgrade adds freshness columns, rebuilds the embeddings table without its foreign key, and recreates its HNSW indexes in one transaction. It preserves chunk IDs so the full-text index remains valid.

### Testing

The full testthat suite was run. Tests cover read-only access, writable upgrades, ingestion, synchronization, and index preservation for older v2 stores.

I also manually compared the tables, constraints, and indexes of an upgraded store with those of a newly created store.

title: Adopt S7 package conventions and fix retrieval examples
description:
ragnar now uses the development version of S7 and its package conventions. The retrieval tool examples in the vignette are also updated for current ellmer.

## Public-facing changes

- `DESCRIPTION` requires `S7 (>= 0.2.2.9000)` and lists `RConsortium/S7` in `Remotes`. Before the next CRAN release, once S7 1.0.0 is on CRAN, the constraint should become `S7 (>= 1.0.0)` and the `Remotes` entry should be removed.
- The retrieval tool examples in `vignette("ragnar")` use `store_description` and pass `store` to `ragnar_retrieve()`. The custom tool returns JSON and declares its arguments with `arguments =`, following changes in ellmer 0.5.0 and 0.3.0.

## Internal changes

- Import `:=` from S7 and remove ragnar's internal copy. Exclude it from the rlang import to avoid a replaced-import warning on load.
- Call `S7_on_load()` from `.onLoad()`, `S7_on_unload()` from `.onUnload()`, and `S7_on_build()` at the top level of `R/zzz.R`.
- Register S7 methods at the top level instead of inside `local()`. `S7_on_build()` removes the placeholders returned by `method<-` for generics owned by other packages.

## Testing

Run against S7 0.2.2.9000 (RConsortium/S7@432d4d1) and ellmer 0.5.1.9000 (tidyverse/ellmer@4e3e6c0):

- `devtools::test()`: 0 failures, 0 warnings, 870 passes, 5 skips (missing credentials).
- `R CMD check --no-tests --no-manual`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.

title: Default embed_ollama() to embeddinggemma-2:270m-q8_0-text
description:
`embed_ollama()` now defaults to `model = "embeddinggemma-2:270m-q8_0-text"`, replacing `embeddinggemma:300m`.

The default names a fixed build rather than `:latest`. A store records the model name, not the weights, so a tag that changes would make query embeddings stop matching the stored ones without an error. `:latest` also resolves to different builds on different machines: on Apple silicon it pulls an MLX `nvfp4` build whose embeddings differ from the `q8_0` build (cosine about 0.99 for the same text).

The 270m text-only build gives identical text embeddings to the 740m build that `:latest` points to (cosine 1.0, maximum absolute difference 0). The larger builds add image and audio modules that `embed_ollama()` does not use. The download is 303 MB, compared with 1.3 GB for `:latest` and 621 MB for the previous default.

Public-facing changes:

- The default model for `embed_ollama()`, and so for `ragnar_store_create()`, which uses `embed_ollama()` by default. Existing stores are unaffected: a store records the embedding function with its model name when it is created. New stores created with the default need `ollama pull embeddinggemma-2:270m-q8_0-text`. NEWS lists this under breaking changes.
- The `ragnar_store_atlas()` example and `examples/chat-with-package.R` use the default model instead of pinning `embeddinggemma:300m-qat-q4_0` and `all-minilm`.

Internal: the snapshot of the stored `embed_ollama()` function records the new model name.

## Testing

- `devtools::test()` for the store and embedding tests, with Ollama running `embeddinggemma-2:270m-q8_0-text` locally: all pass.
- Embedded 6 queries and 6 passages with `270m-q8_0-text`, `740m-q8_0`, and `latest`: all return 768-dimensional vectors and rank the matching passage first for every query.

title: Use ellmer's default OpenAI chat model in examples
description:
